title: Island Hopping From Samobor, Croatia: 2027 Guide
metaDescription: Samobor is inland with no islands. Here is how to reach Brač, Hvar and Vis from Samobor, with 2027 ferry costs, travel times and local tips.
content:
## Is There Island Hopping in Samobor?

No. Samobor is a town of about 14,000 residents in Zagreb County, at the foot of the Samobor Hills (Samoborsko gorje). The nearest sea is the Adriatic coast at Rijeka, about 150 km away. The nearest islands are Krk and Cres in the north, and the Dalmatian islands around Split in the south.

Travelers searching for island hopping from Samobor usually want one of two things: a plan that starts from a Samobor base, or a way to combine the town with the Adriatic. Both are possible. The practical route is to treat Samobor as a quiet start or end point and do the island hopping from Split.

## How to Get From Samobor to the Islands

### Step 1: Samobor to Zagreb (25 km, about 40 minutes)

Buses run between Samobor and Zagreb's main bus station throughout the day, and there is also a local tram-and-bus link into the city. The drive on the A3/Zagreb ring road takes 25 to 35 minutes outside rush hour. Samobor is also close to the Slovenian border at Bregana, which makes it a convenient first or last night on a route from Ljubljana or Graz.

### Step 2: Zagreb to Split (about 410 km)

| Option | Time | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Car via A1 motorway | 4 to 5 hours | Motorway tolls apply. Summer Saturdays are the slowest. |
| Intercity bus | 5 to 6 hours | Several daily departures from Zagreb bus station. |
| Flight Zagreb to Split | About 45 minutes | Fastest option. Split Airport is about 25 km from the ferry port. |

A car is not needed for island hopping. Foot passengers can use the catamarans, and cars on the islands are expensive to ferry. Leave the car in a secure garage in Split or at Zagreb Airport if you are flying.

### Step 3: Split port to the islands

All main routes leave from Split's harbour in the city center, a short walk from the bus and train stations. Jadrolinija is the state operator. Kapetan Luka (Krilo) and TP Line run private fast boats.

## Island Hopping Route From Split: Brač, Hvar and Vis

The standard three-island chain works because catamarans link the islands to each other without returning to Split.

### Brač (start here)

The car ferry from Split to Supetar takes about 50 minutes and costs about €6.50 per adult, with up to 14 sailings a day in high season. Bol, on the south coast, has the Zlatni Rat pebble beach, which is the main reason to cross. Bol is reached more directly by the Jadrolinija catamaran line 9603, which takes about 1 hour 5 minutes and costs €10 per adult in peak season (29 May to 27 September) and €6.40 outside it. Book ahead in summer, because this line is subsidised and tickets are tied to a departure.

### Hvar

The catamaran from Split to Hvar Town takes about one hour and costs roughly €15 to €25 depending on operator and boat. The cheaper Krilo service that calls at Milna on Brač on the way costs around €15. The car ferry from Split to Stari Grad takes about two hours and costs €8.40 per adult in high season (€5.90 off-season), with a standard car at €47.60. Stari Grad is a quieter base than Hvar Town and sits next to the UNESCO-listed Stari Grad Plain, a farmland landscape laid out by Greek settlers in the 4th century BC.

### Vis

Vis was a closed military zone until 1989 and remains the least developed of the three. Catamaran line 659 links Split, Bol, Hvar and Vis, with the Hvar to Vis leg costing about €25 in high season. The crossing from Hvar is around an hour. Allow at least two nights, since the day trips from Split are short on time on the island itself.

### Suggested 7-day plan

| Day | Plan |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Samobor to Zagreb, then flight or drive to Split |
| 2 | Split to Bol (Brač), beach and sunset at Zlatni Rat |
| 3 | Bol to Hvar Town by catamaran |
| 4 | Hvar Town to Stari Grad, walk the plain |
| 5 | Hvar to Vis by catamaran |
| 6 | Vis, then boat back toward Split |
| 7 | Return to Zagreb and Samobor |

## Cost of an Island-Hopping Trip Starting in Samobor

Transport for the Brač, Hvar and Vis chain is modest when using public boats. Four sea legs (Split to Bol, Bol to Hvar, Hvar to Vis, Vis back to Split) cost about €80 to €100 per person in high season. Add the Samobor to Zagreb bus and a Zagreb to Split flight or bus, and total transport usually lands between €130 and €200 per person.

A private water taxi is the alternative when public boats are full. Per boat, Split to Brač runs about €270 to €900, Split to Hvar about €370 to €900, and Split to Vis about €460 to €1,000. The price per person falls to catamaran levels only if the boat is full with 8 to 12 people.

Skip the private water taxi unless your group has eight or more people or you have missed the last catamaran. For one or two travelers it costs ten times the ticket for the same crossing.

## What to Do in Samobor Before or After the Islands

Samobor is worth a night at either end of the trip. It is a compact baroque town, walkable in two hours, and sits at the entrance to the Žumberak-Samobor Hills Nature Park.

### Town highlights

- **Main Square (Trg kralja Tomislava):** pastel facades, the Church of St. Anastasia and the town hall. This is where the Samobor carnival (Fašnik) parades run each winter.
- **Samoborska kremšnita:** the town's cream cake, a thick custard and whipped-cream slice on a thin pastry base. Cafés on the main square sell it for roughly €3 to €4. Eat it fresh in the morning, when it is at its best.
- **Samobor mustard and bermet:** Samobor mustard is a local product sold in small jars for a few euros. Bermet is a spiced, sweet aperitif wine made in the area.
- **Old Town castle ruins (Stari grad Samobor):** a 20-minute uphill walk from the center to a 13th-century hilltop fortress with views over the town and the Sava valley.
- **Town museum:** the Samobor Museum (Gradski muzej Samobor) holds local history and regional collections.

### Hiking and wine

Japetić (879 m) is the highest nearby summit and has a mountain lodge. The path to the peak starts at the edge of Samobor and takes about 2.5 to 3 hours one way for an average walker. The Plešivica wine road, 15 km to the south, covers family cellars producing sparkling and white wines. A sparkling wine tasting is a good last-night alternative to a coastal restaurant.

## Best Time to Go

| Season | Island conditions | Samobor conditions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| May to June | Warm, fewer crowds, lower fares | Good hiking, café terraces open |
| July to August | Full timetable, up to 19 daily Split to Hvar sailings, tickets sell out | Hot but mild in the hills |
| September | Sea still warm, lower prices | Grape harvest in Plešivica |
| October to April | 2 to 3 daily Split to Hvar sailings, many seasonal catamarans stop | Carnival in February, quiet streets |

The best window is late May to mid-June or mid-September. Fares are lower than in July and August, and the 2026 off-season ticket on line 9603 is €6.40 against €10 in peak season.

## Local Tips

- **Buy catamaran tickets 2 to 3 days ahead in July and August.** Boarding closes about 10 minutes before departure.
- **Bring cash for small island cafés.** Card machines are common but not universal on Vis and in Hvar's smaller villages.
- **Luggage:** the catamaran charges roughly €5 per large bag on some lines. Pack in one carry-on bag if you plan three or more island legs.
- **Do not rely on the last boat.** Last departures from Hvar Town leave around 20:30 in peak weeks. A missed boat means a night's accommodation or a €370 or higher water taxi.
- **Save a night in Samobor at the end.** Returning from Split on a late flight into Zagreb then a 25 km transfer is easier with a Samobor bed than a 2 a.m. arrival in the city.

## Alternatives: Closer Islands From the North

From Samobor, Krk is the nearest island, about 190 km away, and connects to the mainland by a road bridge, so no ferry is needed. Cres and Lošinj, farther along the Kvarner coast, need a short ferry from Brestova to Porozina. These work for a long weekend but do not give the hop-between-islands feel of the Dalmatian chain.

faq.question: Are there islands near Samobor, Croatia?
faq.answer: No. Samobor is an inland town 25 km west of Zagreb with no sea or islands. The nearest island is Krk, about 190 km away, and it is reached by a road bridge.

faq.question: How do you get from Samobor to the Croatian islands?
faq.answer: Take a bus or drive 25 km to Zagreb, then travel about 410 km to Split by car, bus or a 45-minute flight. From Split, catamarans and car ferries leave for Brač, Hvar and Vis.

faq.question: How much does island hopping from Split cost?
faq.answer: Public boats cost about €6.50 to €25 per leg depending on route and season. A four-leg Brač, Hvar and Vis loop is roughly €80 to €100 per person in high season.

faq.question: How long does the ferry from Split to Hvar take?
faq.answer: The catamaran to Hvar Town takes about one hour, and the car ferry to Stari Grad takes about two hours. Catamaran fares are around €15 to €25, while the car ferry is €8.40 per adult in high season.

faq.question: Do you need a car for island hopping in Croatia?
faq.answer: No. Foot passengers can use the catamarans between Split, Brač, Hvar and Vis, and local buses and taxis cover the islands. A car on the Hvar ferry costs about €47.60 each way in summer, so leave it behind.

faq.question: When is the best time for island hopping from Samobor?
faq.answer: Late May to mid-June and September are the best months. Crowds are smaller, fares are lower, and the sea is warm enough to swim. July and August have the most sailings but also sell out.

faq.question: Is Samobor worth visiting on an island trip?
faq.answer: Yes, as a one-night stop before or after the coast. The old town, kremšnita cake, Japetić hike and Plešivica wine road are all within 15 km, and Zagreb Airport is about 35 km away.

quickAnswer: Samobor has no islands or coastline. It is an inland town 25 km west of Zagreb. To island-hop, travel about 410 km to Split (4 to 5 hours by road, or a 45-minute flight from Zagreb), then take ferries or catamarans to Brač, Hvar and Vis for €6 to €25 per leg.
